html-a01-global-attributes.q: A form's error summary must receive focus from JavaScript after a failed submit, but should never be a Tab stop. Which markup is correct?
options: <section id="errors" tabindex="0">
<section id="errors" tabindex="-1">
<section id="errors" tabindex="1">
<section id="errors" accesskey="e">
html-a01-global-attributes.why: tabindex="-1" makes an element focusable by script (element.focus()) while keeping it out of the Tab order; 0 would add a useless Tab stop and positive values scramble the sequence.

html-a01-global-attributes.q: An English page displays user-submitted chat messages that may arrive in Hebrew or English. How should each message element handle text direction?
options: dir="rtl" on the html element
dir="ltr" on every message to keep the layout stable
dir="auto" on each message element
No dir attribute — browsers detect direction from the font
html-a01-global-attributes.why: dir="auto" makes the browser inspect each element's first strongly directional character and set ltr or rtl per message — the only approach that works for unpredictable user content.

html-a01-global-attributes.q: A tooltip explaining an icon's meaning is provided only via the title attribute. Who reliably never sees that information?
options: Desktop users with a mouse
Users of Chromium-based browsers
Touch-screen and keyboard-only users
Users with the page zoomed to 200%
html-a01-global-attributes.why: The title tooltip appears on pointer hover only: touch screens have no hover and keyboard focus does not trigger it, so critical information must exist as visible text or an accessible name instead.

html-a02-data-attributes.q: Your JavaScript needs to read el.dataset.maxRetries. Which attribute must the HTML carry?
options: data-maxRetries="3"
data-max-retries="3"
max-retries="3"
dataset-max-retries="3"
html-a02-data-attributes.why: dataset camelCases the kebab-case name after the data- prefix, so dataset.maxRetries maps to data-max-retries; uppercase in the attribute itself is lowercased by the parser and breaks the mapping.

html-a02-data-attributes.q: A card must show whether an event is upcoming or past, and screen-reader users need machine-readable timing too. What is the right markup for the date?
options: Sept 1
<time datetime="2026-09-01">Sept 1</time>
Sept 1
Sept 1
html-a02-data-attributes.why: When HTML has a native element for the meaning — time with datetime — using data-* instead throws away real semantics; data attributes are only for information no standard feature covers.

html-a02-data-attributes.q: A filter script hides products by comparing li.dataset.price > 50. It never matches anything, even for a li with data-price="89". Why?
options: dataset only works on div elements
The attribute should be named data-Price
dataset values are strings, so the comparison needs Number(li.dataset.price)
data-price is reserved by HTML for commerce metadata
html-a02-data-attributes.why: Every dataset value is a string; "89" > 50 relies on coercion quirks and equality checks fail outright, so numeric data must be converted with Number() before comparing.

html-a03-responsive-images.q: A hero image renders 100vw wide on phones and 800px elsewhere, with candidates at 400w/800w/1600w. A 400px-wide viewport at device pixel ratio 2 loads which file, and why?
options: hero-400.jpg — the viewport is 400px wide
hero-800.jpg — 400 CSS px × 2 DPR needs ~800 image pixels
hero-1600.jpg — browsers always take the largest candidate
hero-800.jpg — the sizes attribute defaults to 800px
html-a03-responsive-images.why: The browser resolves sizes to 400 CSS pixels, multiplies by DPR 2 to get a needed width of ~800 pixels, and downloads the smallest candidate at or above it: the 800w file.

html-a03-responsive-images.q: You must show a wide landscape crop on desktop but a tight square crop on phones — genuinely different files. Which mechanism is correct?
options: srcset with x descriptors on one img
srcset with w descriptors plus sizes on one img
picture with source media="(max-width: 600px)" for the square crop
Two img elements toggled with the hidden attribute
html-a03-responsive-images.why: Changing the crop is art direction — an editorial decision the browser must obey — which is exactly what picture's media-based source selection is for; srcset only scales the same picture.

html-a03-responsive-images.q: After adding loading="lazy" to every image sitewide, the homepage's Largest Contentful Paint got worse. What happened?
options: lazy also disables srcset selection
The above-the-fold hero now waits for layout before fetching, delaying the largest paint
decoding="async" is required for lazy to work
Lazy images always load at 1x resolution first
html-a03-responsive-images.why: Lazy loading removes an image from the preload scanner's early fetch, so applying it to first-screen images delays exactly the paint LCP measures — above-the-fold images must load eagerly.

html-a04-seo-social-meta.q: A marketing URL shared in Slack shows no image and the bare domain, though the page looks fine in a browser. The og: tags are injected by client-side React. What is the actual problem?
options: Slack only supports Twitter card tags
Link scrapers do not execute JavaScript, so client-injected tags are invisible to them
og:image must be a relative URL
The page is missing a favicon
html-a04-seo-social-meta.why: Preview scrapers read the server-delivered HTML once and never run scripts, so Open Graph tags must be present in the initial markup (server-rendered or prerendered).

html-a04-seo-social-meta.q: The same article is reachable at /guide, /guide?utm_source=mail and /Guide. What single head element consolidates ranking signals onto one URL?
options: <meta name="robots" content="noindex"> on the variants
<link rel="canonical" href="https://site.example/guide">
<meta property="og:url" content="/guide">
<base href="https://site.example/guide">
html-a04-seo-social-meta.why: rel=canonical declares the one official URL for duplicated content so engines merge the variants' signals; noindex would remove pages from search rather than consolidate them.

html-a04-seo-social-meta.q: A production page vanished from Google weeks after launch. The head contains <meta name="robots" content="noindex"> left over from staging. What does that tag do?
options: It only blocks the page's images from image search
It is advisory — engines usually ignore it
It directs engines to drop the page from search results entirely
It merely hides the meta description snippet
html-a04-seo-social-meta.why: robots noindex is a directive, not a hint: compliant engines deindex the page, which is why leftover staging meta tags are a classic and costly launch bug.

html-a05-accessibility-alt-headings.q: A purely decorative divider image sits between article sections. What is the correct markup?
html-a05-accessibility-alt-headings.why: The explicit empty alt tells screen readers to skip the image silently; omitting the attribute makes them fall back to announcing the filename, and describing decoration adds noise.

html-a05-accessibility-alt-headings.q: A designer hides the 'Skip to content' link with display: none, revealing it via a hover class. Why is the feature now broken?
options: Skip links must be buttons, not anchors
display: none removes the link from the Tab order, so keyboard users can never reach it
The link needs aria-hidden="true" as well
Hover styles are not allowed on anchors
html-a05-accessibility-alt-headings.why: A skip link works by being the first Tab stop and appearing on focus; display: none removes it from the tab order entirely, so it must be hidden off-screen and revealed with :focus.

html-a05-accessibility-alt-headings.q: The same portrait photo appears on a team page and in an article about studio lighting. What is true about its alt text?
options: It should be identical in both places for consistency
It depends on context: the person's name on the team page, the lighting technique in the article
Both should use the filename so they stay in sync
The article copy needs no alt because the caption describes it
html-a05-accessibility-alt-headings.why: Alt text conveys what the image contributes in its context, so one file legitimately gets different descriptions on different pages — and a caption comments on an image rather than replacing it.

html-a06-aria.q: A developer adds role="button" and aria-label="Save" to a div with a click handler. A keyboard user Tabs toward it. What happens?
options: It works — role="button" makes Enter and Space activate it
Focus skips it entirely: ARIA changes announcements, never focusability or behavior
It receives focus but only Space works
The browser converts it to a native button internally
html-a06-aria.why: ARIA only edits the accessibility tree; the div still needs tabindex="0" and hand-written Enter/Space key handling — which is why the first rule of ARIA says to use a native button instead.

html-a06-aria.q: A section's visible heading should serve as its accessible name for screen readers. Which wiring is best?
options: aria-label="Billing address" on the section
aria-describedby pointing at the heading's id
aria-labelledby on the section pointing at the heading's id
title="Billing address" on the section
html-a06-aria.why: aria-labelledby reuses on-screen text as the name, so it cannot drift out of date and gets translated; aria-label duplicates the string invisibly and describedby supplies description, not the name.

html-a06-aria.q: A save confirmation ('Draft saved') is written into a status element by script, but screen readers say nothing. The element was created by the same script that sets its text. What is the robust fix?
options: Switch the message to aria-live="assertive"
Keep an empty aria-live="polite" element in the DOM from page load and update its text
Move focus to the status element on every save
Use aria-hidden="false" on the message
html-a06-aria.why: Screen readers register live regions when the tree is first built; a region injected together with its message is often missed, so the container must pre-exist empty and receive only text updates.

html-a07-keyboard-focus.q: A brand stylesheet contains * { outline: none } because the focus ring 'looked ugly'. What is the professional fix?
options: Delete all focus styling permanently — rings are optional
Add a :focus-visible rule with a styled outline so keyboard users get an indicator while mouse clicks stay ring-free
Replace outlines with title tooltips on focus
Set tabindex="-1" on all controls so focus is never visible
html-a07-keyboard-focus.why: :focus-visible shows the indicator only for keyboard-driven focus, satisfying both the designer's complaint about click rings and WCAG's requirement that keyboard focus be visible.

html-a07-keyboard-focus.q: The visual design places the Save button left of Cancel, but the DOM has Cancel first, so Tab reaches Cancel before Save. What is the correct repair?
options: tabindex="1" on Save and tabindex="2" on Cancel
Reorder the buttons in the source so DOM order matches visual order
tabindex="0" on Save only
aria-flowto on the Save button
html-a07-keyboard-focus.why: Natural tab order follows source order; fixing the source keeps everything maintainable, whereas positive tabindex values create a fragile parallel order that breaks on the next change.

html-a07-keyboard-focus.q: An icon-only bold button must announce as 'Bold' but show only the letter B. Which pattern is correct?
options: <button title="Bold">B</button>
<button aria-hidden="true">Bold</button>
html-a07-keyboard-focus.why: The icon is silenced with aria-hidden while the sr-only span supplies real, translatable name text hidden by clipping — display:none would hide it from screen readers too, and title is unreliable.

html-a08-details-dialog.q: A settings page needs an accordion where opening one section automatically closes the others, with no JavaScript. Which markup achieves it?
options: Several <details> elements sharing the same name attribute
Several <details> elements sharing the same class
One <details> wrapping all the sections
<details exclusive> on each section
html-a08-details-dialog.why: Like radio buttons, details elements with a shared name form an exclusive group: the browser closes the open member whenever another opens.

html-a08-details-dialog.q: A confirmation box appears via <dialog open> in the markup, but users can still click the page behind it and Tab escapes the box. Why?
options: The dialog is missing aria-modal
The open attribute (and show()) presents a dialog non-modally; only showModal() makes the page inert, traps focus and enables the ::backdrop
dialog only becomes modal inside a form
Escape handling must be added before modality activates
html-a08-details-dialog.why: Modality is decided by how the dialog is shown: showModal() delivers the inert background, focus trap, Escape support and backdrop, while the open attribute always yields a non-modal box.

html-a08-details-dialog.q: A 'Filters' button should toggle a floating panel that closes when the user clicks anywhere else, without blocking the page. Which primitive fits?
options: A dialog opened with showModal()
A details element wrapping the panel
A div with the popover attribute, toggled by the button's popovertarget
A hidden div toggled by removing the hidden attribute
html-a08-details-dialog.why: Light-dismiss floating overlays are the popover attribute's exact use case: top-layer rendering, outside-click and Escape dismissal, and pure-HTML wiring via popovertarget — no modality, no script.
